note: Block List Override filters block plugin definitions out of Drupal's block library via hook_block_alter (site-wide list) and hook_plugin_filter_block__layout_builder_alter (Layout Builder chooser). Config object block_list_override.settings holds system_match/system_prefix/system_regex (newline-separated strings) and system_negate (0=Remove matched, 1=Allow only matched), plus layout_* keys (layout_match/prefix/regex are saved by the form but NOT used by the alter hooks in 1.0.x; only layout_negate is distinct). Matching (BlockListOverride::blockIsAllowed): exact match, colon-prefix (id starts '<prefix>:'), or regex preg_match; blocks already placed in Layout Builder sections are never removed. Settings at /admin/config/block_list_override/settings (permission 'access block list override'). Medium cases read back a known system_match and system_prefix value; hard cases actually remove the core system_powered_by_block block (verified by it disappearing from the live block plugin definitions) via exact match and via regex.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with block_list_override enabled, which configuration object and keys control which blocks are removed from the block list, and at what admin path do I configure it?
evals.expected_output: Config object block_list_override.settings with keys system_match, system_prefix, system_regex and system_negate (plus layout_* variants). Configure at /admin/config/block_list_override/settings (permission 'access block list override').

evals.prompt: Block List Override lets me target blocks three different ways. What are the three matching methods, and how does the prefix method decide a block matches?
evals.expected_output: Match (exact plugin id), Prefix (the plugin id starts with '<prefix>:', e.g. field_block:user matches field_block:user:user:uid), and Regex (preg_match against the plugin id, e.g. /field_block:node:(.*):nid/). Each list is one entry per line.

evals.prompt: Instead of removing a few blocks, I want Block List Override to keep ONLY a chosen set of blocks and drop everything else. Which setting controls that, and are blocks already placed in Layout Builder still protected?
evals.expected_output: Set the Action to 'Allow only' (system_negate = 1); then only listed blocks are kept and everything else is removed (negate = 0 is the default 'Remove' behaviour). Blocks already used in a Layout Builder section are always kept regardless, to avoid breaking existing layouts.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, Block List Override is configured to remove a specific block by exact match. Inspect the live configuration and give the block plugin id that is being removed.
evals.expected_output: block_list_override.settings:system_match is 'system_powered_by_block' with system_negate = 0 (Remove), so the Powered by Drupal block is removed.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, Block List Override is configured to remove a whole family of blocks by prefix. Inspect the live configuration and state which prefix is configured.
evals.expected_output: block_list_override.settings:system_prefix is 'views_block' with system_negate = 0, so all blocks whose id starts with 'views_block:' are removed.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, remove the core 'Powered by Drupal' block (plugin id system_powered_by_block) from the block list using the block_list_override module (exact match), and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set block_list_override.settings:system_match to 'system_powered_by_block' with system_negate = 0 (Remove) and rebuild caches. The verify checks that system_powered_by_block is no longer in the block plugin definitions and that it is listed in system_match.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the block_list_override module's regex option to remove the 'Powered by Drupal' block (plugin id system_powered_by_block) from the block list, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set block_list_override.settings:system_regex to a pattern matching the id (e.g. /^system_powered_by_block$/ or /powered_by/) with system_negate = 0, and rebuild caches. The verify checks system_powered_by_block is gone from the block plugin definitions and that a non-empty system_regex is configured.
